title: Double the width, double the area
summary: A rectangle widens while its height stays fixed. Labels and an added strip connect the motion to its area.
learningObjective: Explain why doubling a rectangle’s width at fixed height doubles its area.

check.question: At the same height, what happens to the area if the original width is tripled?
check.answer: The area triples: three equal strips fit beside one another.

uncertain: May not connect multiplication to a changing rectangle.

teaching.focus: Connect a width change to the additional equal area.
teaching.approach: Keep the original rectangle visible and add one equal strip.
teaching.pacing: Explain the original dimensions, animate during the width change, then hold the comparison.

changes: Preserved the original rectangle and fixed height throughout the widening.
limitations: Diagram lengths are schematic; voice and duration vary with speech settings.

scenes.title: Change one dimension

beats.narration: This rectangle is three centimeters wide and two centimeters high. Its area is six square centimeters.
Keep the height fixed and double the width. Watch the added strip: it has the same area as the original rectangle.
The width is now six centimeters. The area is twelve square centimeters. Doubling just the width doubles the area.
